Magical gene / fields and regions

Collar

A band right round the base of the neck, with everything behind it going pale and the head, crest and lower legs keeping the coat.

What it does

CollarThe band wraps the whole circumference at the base of the neck, its back edge landing at or near the front of the scapula, and it divides the horse: everything behind it goes pale, roughly half the animal, while the head, the front of the neck and the crest keep their colour. The legs come back to the coat from the knee and hock down, over a soft transition rather than a line. The mane keeps its colour; the tail follows the pale field about half the time.
Coloured collarThe same split, with the caudal field in a colour rather than pale. Fully recessive: two copies, and a single copy beside the white allele shows white. It never gives blue eyes.
Wild typeNo collar.

What you can get

Finding one

About 1 in 1,786 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

Its gene carrot

The file

common/src/main/resources/horsegenetics/genes/collar.json — a data-driven gene, not a Java class. It is listed in the index.json beside it and registered by Genes' class initialiser at startup.

Keyhorsegenetics.collar
Phasemagical — it adds signed colour in phase 3, after the pigment has resolved
Priority260 — where it sits in the one (priority, key) paint order
AllelesCol · Coc · n
Varies per horse2 values drawn once off the expressing allele copy, so a foal that inherits the copy inherits the look
Built fromAXIS, TOWARD

What it paints

Collar

  1. everything behind the collar — AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  2. the legs coming back to the coat below the knee — AXIS, painted with TOWARD

Coloured collar

  1. everything behind the collar, coloured — AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  2. the legs, coloured to the knee — AXIS, painted with TOWARD
